text: ('gdn_reg', {'invitation': 'You are invited to register for a Zoom webinar! When: Nov 25, 2026 11:00 AM Eastern Time (US and Canada) Topic: Advancing Trust in Academic Recognition: Verification, Digitalisation and the Future Role of AI in Armenia Register in advance for this webinar: https://us02web.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_tyMRc1NyR22mjURkbOAhXg After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about joining the webinar. ---------- Webinar Speakers Gayané Harutyunyan (General Director @National Information Center for Academic Recognition and Mobility (ArmEnic)) Joanne Duklas (Executive Director @The GDN Network) Joanne Duklas is an award-winning leader in higher education who serves as the executive director of the GDN Network while also leading scholarly research projects and her own consulting firm in higher education providing research and consulting support to governments, institutions, and sector organizations. She most recently served as one of the co-founders and executive lead for the MyCreds™ | MesCertif™ National Network in Canada. She is an expert in the higher education field and has authored several publications, presentations, and keynote addresses to advance best practice, standards, transfer, and student mobility including recent chapter contributions on digitization, trust, privacy, and fraud in the Second Handbook on Academic Integrity and Fake Degrees and Fraudulent Credentials in Higher Education. Ani Hovhannisyan (International Relations & Strategic Development Coordinator @National Information Center for Academic Recognition and Mobility (ArmEnic)) Ani Hovhannisyan is the International Relations and Strategic Development Coordinator at the Armenian National Information Center for Academic Recognition and Mobility (ArmENIC). She has over 14 years of professional experience in higher education, with expertise in academic mobility, internationalisation and higher education policy. Her professional background encompasses national and European-level policy development, institutional leadership, research and international cooperation, including experience in representing Armenia in various international and European higher education working groups, expert platforms and professional networks. Throughout her career at ArmENIC, she has contributed to international projects, research and publications in the field of academic recognition and higher education. Her professional interests focus on strengthening trust in academic credentials and fostering international cooperation.
